assets.post:
Masters are used unchanged. `hlasset build-screens` scales them into the screen catalog's `capture`
family: `capture/depot`, `capture/factory` and `capture/hand` 512 px wide at 1x and 1024 at 2x,
`capture/hq` and `capture/hq-open` to the full screen, 640x400 at 1x and 1280x800 at 2x, and the
three surrender paintings likewise to the full screen (`capture/surrender`,
`capture/surrender-offer`, `capture/surrender-accepted`). `internal/dospanel` plays the surrender
as held frames with crossfades (fade in, offer, acceptance, hold); under reduced motion it shows
the acceptance at once.
`internal/dospanel` places the code-drawn parts by points measured on the masters, as fractions of
their size: the pin goes into the depot's roof ridge at 0.624, 0.303 and the factory's at 0.526,
0.300; the hand pinches at 0.184, 0.218; the HQ's flagpole stands at 0.500 from 0.199 (foot) to
0.050 (head); the door leaves fill the arch from 0.413 to 0.586 wide, from 0.474 (crown) and 0.544
(springing) down to 0.832. A new master must keep these points or change them in code. The map room
is drawn at the scene's light, the hand toned to sepia; the leaves of `hq.png` swing open over
`hq-open.png`.

assets.post:
Masters are used unchanged. `hlasset build-screens` scales each into the screen catalog's `surface`
family: `surface/steel` and `surface/ground` at 512 px at 1x and 1024 px at 2x, wrapping so the tile
stays seamless, and `surface/rivets` at 512x256 at 1x and 1024x512 at 2x. `internal/dospanel` grades
the tiles to its palette: only each texel's colour relative to the tile's mean shows, so colour drift in
a master does not matter. One steel tile spans 256 reference pixels of a panel, one ground tile 96. The
rivet heads keep their painted hue, brightened evenly so their mean is as light as the panel's brass.
Each head is cut out of its cell by a circle of its measured centre and radius, which drops the sheet's
faint alpha haze; the rivet's shadow is drawn in code.

`surface/plate` and `surface/plate-2` to `-4` are scaled like a tile (512 px wide at 1x, 1024 px at 2x).
`internal/dosscreen` takes each one's opaque box (alpha over half) as the cell's 96x80 box and draws a
plate, unchanged in colour, on every cell of a panel frame that is not an opening, over the darkest
steel, so the teeth are plates with seams between them; a dark lip is drawn along the openings. Each
cell picks its plate by its place in the view. The chrome around the panels (the divider post, the
steel strips and the bolt) takes the plates' mean colour, with `surface/steel` graded on it as on the
panels.

`surface/newsprint` is scaled like a tile (512 px at 1x, 1024 px at 2x) and tiled unchanged over the
campaign newspaper's sheet.

assets.title: Harbour
assets.look:
A small harbour of 1910 on three hexes paved with grey granite setts: a long brick quayside warehouse with
a slate roof and four hoist dormers, its ridge north-south; at its SW a small stone customs house with a red
clay tile hipped roof, two chimneys and an open timber coal bunker; at its S the quay yard with a hand crane
on a granite base, its jib reaching east over the water, stacked crates, barrels and jute sacks, where the
road comes in from the south. In winter snow lies on the roofs and the cargo, and old trodden snow with slush
patches on the setts. It stands where the original maps have their harbour (records 53, 52 and 120), which
the levels keep as two houses carrying harbourN and harbourW and a road carrying harbourS.
assets.base_prompt:
A transparent cut-out sheet in three columns, strict nadir, no ground, no cast shadow: the warehouse, the
yard's crane and cargo, the customs house; and an opaque, even granite sett paving of a quay yard.

The warehouse, the customs house and the yard's crane and cargo, summer and winter.
Their cast shadows, made in code.

`TestGenerateHarbourTiles` (`tools/art-review`, tag `campaigngfx`) samples the paving at 6 source px per

yard 80 S), so the setts run on over the edges the three hexes share. Along the outer edges the paving fades
out over 5 world px behind a margin of 2 to 6 world px that wanders (smooth noise over 10 world px), with
the corners rounded; at the yard's S edge it leaves the road uncovered for 8 world px and fades in over it
slowly, so the road runs into the yard. The kit's pieces are the opaque shapes whose centre lies in a

its hex centre, the customs house 32 wide at its centre, the yard's cargo 40 wide at 17 E and 6 N of the
yard's centre, the crane jib reaching over the NE edge. Each casts a code-made shadow 2.5 world px toward
the lower right; a piece and its shadow are cut to the logical pixels they cover, with the anchor moved to
match, which keeps the standing pack within its decoded budget.

```text

A 1916 front-line fire trench runs left to right along y=512 as a crenellated trace: straight fire bays 128 px long alternate with square traverses 43 px long, the trace stepping 32 px up and down (exactly 6 bays across the width). Trench floor 75 px wide: dark wet umber clay with timber duckboards along the centre; walls revetted with weathered planks and wattle on the shaded side. On the upper (enemy) side a parapet bank 64 px wide of tan-brown spoil topped with a rim of grey-brown sandbags; on the lower side a lower parados 53 px wide of spoil with clods. The banks fade into churned meadow with a few shell-scarred bare patches, then olive meadow. The inner wall facing the lower right is in deep soft shadow. Upper-left light.
